reproducibility.produced_by: generators/prove_mtv2_reproducibility.py -- this file. The digest and the method are emitted together by the script that computed them (BUILD_RULES 9.3, 11.7); no digest in this project is typed by hand.
reproducibility.digest_method: sha256 of each file's bytes, then sha256 over the sorted lines '<relative path> <per-file digest>'. A rename, an addition, a deletion and a content change are each visible.
reproducibility.named_file_set: every file under models/, plus dbt_project.yml and packages.yml
reproducibility.never_deleted: build_artifacts/reports/ -- not deleted and not backed up (BUILD_RULES 9.3). BUILD_STATUS.json is also not deleted: it carries another stage's clause block, it is not in the digested set, and selfcheck_mtv2.py rewrites every key it owns and fails on a preserved count that no longer describes the tree.

foreign_block_preservation_proof.note: stage 2's clause block is written into this same file. A re-run used to discard it; it is preserved now, and selfcheck FAILS if a preserved count no longer describes the tree, which was proved separately by planting one.

findings.detail: BD1-FK-HOP-IS-ONE-JOIN -- spine[FOREIGN_KEY -> V].COL emits ONE join on the document handle (v.foreign_key = b.foreign_key), not a per-level climb through the parent chain. WHY: The map's own keynorm log shows the mapper COLLAPSED multi-hop PARENT_KEY_HASH climbs into this one-hop form (class 'chain_to_fkjoin'); expanding it back into a climb would undo the mapper's normalisation, which the builder does not do (BUILD_RULES 5.7). COST: If FOREIGN_KEY is a file/batch handle rather than a document handle, the join fans out and every key built on it is WRONG rather than empty. Open item P6-FK-ROUNDTRIP; 863 spine occurrences depend on it and there is no sample data in this run. The per-view diagnostic in audit_mtv2_fk_roundtrip falsifies it before any load. TO OVERRULE: set FK_HOP_MODE = 'parent_chain' in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD2-FK-INTERVENING-CASTS-PROVISIONED -- The cast layer covers every view on the PARENT CHAIN between a hop's start and its named destination, including the levels a FOREIGN_KEY hop skips and therefore never joins under BD1. WHY: BUILD_RULES 6.1 sizes the cast layer by whether a view is on a walk, and the profile sizes it the same way (97 destinations-only -> 113 expanded). Provisioning them also makes BD1 reversible without adding a model. COST: A handful of cast models are referenced by no resolver while FK_HOP_MODE is 'document_handle'. They are counted and named in the build report so they are not mistaken for dead models. TO OVERRULE: set CAST_COVERAGE = 'joined_only' in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD3-PIVOT-PARENT-IS-THE-BASE-NODE -- On a *_PIVOT_VW, PARENT_KEY_HASH is resolved to the view's own BASE NODE (the index's parent_table_candidate), and every hop is then expanded through that chain. WHY: Open item SPINE-WALK-DISAGREEMENT. 00_tables_index.json is the only physical statement available -- sample_data_available is false -- and it makes the pivot's parent its base node. Expanding every hop through the chain makes the two readings agree for the 697 arrows that NAME the base node; only the first hop of the others is in question. COST: If PARENT_KEY_HASH actually points past the base node, up to 1464 spine slots resolve one level short and mint a second population in HUB_RISK_OBJECT / HUB_PARTY / HUB_POLICY. audit_mtv2_spine_variants counts rows reached by each variant per (view, join column) so one source answer applies in one pass. TO OVERRULE: set PIVOT_PARENT = 'grandparent' in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD4-LNK-LEG-CORROBORATION-IS-REPORTED-NOT-FATAL -- A LNK leg is rendered by the SAME render_key() as a hub key, so it is byte-identical by construction. Where the leg's expression is ALSO used as a standalone hub key on the same view the binding is corroborated; where it is not, the leg is still built and the absence is REPORTED. WHY: The profile's mechanism says 'assert every LNK leg string appears verbatim as some hub resolved_key.expression on that view; raise on any that does not'. Measured: 62 of 91 legs corroborate, 8 are pure role-code literals (not hub keys at all), 21 have no on-view hub key to compare against. Raising would drop 21 real link legs and the loss would read as a source gap -- the exact failure BUILD_RULES 2 documents. COST: 21 legs are built on the mapper's word alone. They are listed individually in the build report, routed to the mapper. TO OVERRULE: set LNK_LEG_UNCORROBORATED = 'fatal' in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD5-ROLE-CODE-IS-A-DEGENERATE-LINK-LEG -- LNK_PARTY_ROLE's second leg is a role CODE ('NOMINEE', 'CUSTOMER', ...), not a hub key -- data_7.js gives LNK_PARTY_ROLE hubs=['HUB_PARTY']. It is carried into the link as a degenerate leg so the link grain is party x role. WHY: Dropping it collapses every role a party plays onto one link row; minting a hub for it invents a hub the model does not have (BUILD_RULES 7.4). COST: The role column in the link table is not a hash key; a consumer joining it to a hub finds none. It IS part of the link hash, so the grain is right. TO OVERRULE: set LINK_DEGENERATE_LEG = 'drop' in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD6-MULTI-ACTIVE-WITHOUT-A-DISCRIMINATOR-IS-SINGLE-ACTIVE -- 277 augmentation rows declare multi_active with no child key in either form. They are built SINGLE-ACTIVE in the augmented track. WHY: A multi-active satellite with no discriminator IS single-active; inventing a child key is model invention (BUILD_RULES 7.4). Leaving them unbuilt would lose 277 of 1291 augmentation rows to a naming gap. COST: If the rows really are multi-valued per parent, the satellite keeps only the last-loaded row per hub key. Every one of the 277 is listed with its proposed child-key NAME in the build report, routed to the mapper. TO OVERRULE: set MA_WITHOUT_CDK = 'unbuilt' in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD7-HASHDIFF-FOLLOWS-THE-SIBLING -- Satellites are written with a BARE HASHDIFF, matching travel_dv_dbt on both tracks (45 of 45, counted). The wide stage still needs a unique name per satellite, so the rename happens in the satfeed view. WHY: BUILD_RULES 7.2/7.7 make the sibling's contract absolute for a satellite it already builds, and 12's shared-vault divergence is exactly what HASHDIFF_<SAT> would re-open here. 27 views feed more than one sibling-built satellite (max 11), so a bare name cannot come from the wide stage itself. COST: One satfeed view per satellite -- a model per satellite that the Maximus house pattern does not have. In exchange BUILD_RULES 12 does not apply to this build. TO OVERRULE: set HASHDIFF_POLICY = 'maximus_house' in mtv2_names.py

BD8-TWO-CONTENT-HASH-CANONICALISATIONS-EMITTED-AS-WRITTEN -- md5(normalise(...)) (128 rows) and md5(upper(trim(...))) (10 rows) are both emitted exactly as mapped. They are NOT unified. WHY: They are used on DISJOINT hubs for different kinds of value -- normalise on HUB_LOCATION (117) and LNK_PARTY_LOCATION (11), all addresses; upper+trim on HUB_PARTY (2) and LNK_PARTY_ROLE (6) nominee NAMES and HUB_ORG_UNIT (2) branch NAMES. Verified: zero hubs carry both forms. Unifying them would re-key a hub on the builder's authority (BUILD_RULES 5.7). COST: For a hand-typed nominee name 'AB  CD' and 'AB CD' stay two parties under the name form and would be one under normalise. That is a modeller call on a hub OPUS also writes, not a build call. Reported, open item MD5-TWO-CANONICALISATIONS. TO OVERRULE: set CONTENT_HASH_UNIFY = True in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD9-DEGENERATE-KEYS-REJECTED-BY-SHAPE-NEVER-BY-CONSTANT -- Every hub and link key is wrapped in a CASE over 'coalesce(<guarded operands>) is not null', then nullif(trim(...),''). An outer nullif(key,'<constant>') is added ONLY where the constant is statically computable. No predicate compares a key to a value from KEY_DEGENERATE_VALUES.csv. WHY: Under Snowflake semantics every one of the map's 2344 key expressions evaluates to NULL on an all-blank row -- including the 369 the CSV calls NON-EMPTY CONSTANT. A predicate key = 'RISK:' can never fire and would read exactly like a working guard. Third instance of that failure in this engagement. COST: None measured. The static-constant branch fires 0 times on this map, and zero is reported as zero -- a guard that never fires proves something about this map, not about the build. TO OVERRULE: set DEGENERATE_OUTER_NULLIF = False in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD10-PURE-LITERAL-KEY-IS-CONSTANT-BY-CONSTRUCTION -- A key expression with no non-literal operand at all is ACCEPTED and emitted as that literal, counted separately. WHY: KEYING.md 9.5 as amended: constant by construction is not degeneration -- there is no operand that can go blank. Refusing it would drop rows for being deterministic. COST: Every row on that view keys to one hub row. That is correct for a single-population namespace and wrong for anything else; the count is printed per hub so it cannot hide. TO OVERRULE: set ACCEPT_CONSTANT_KEY = False in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD11-ANCHOR-ONLY-ROWS-BIND-TO-THE-MAP-S-OWN-KEY -- 190 blocks carry an ANCHOR but no resolved_key at all. They are bound to the key slot the MAP ITSELF resolved for that anchor on the SAME VIEW -- by instance where the row names one, by the satellite's own placement next, by the single candidate next, and by the DOMINANT instance last. WHY: Dropping them is a silence no other check can see: the attribute is never in coverage's denominator, so coverage reads complete over an attribute that was never built (BUILD_RULES 8.1). No key is invented -- every slot used was resolved by the mapper for that anchor on that view. COST: The last rule is an assumption. On one view 101 augmentation attributes name HUB_PARTY with no instance while the map resolves a proposer key (129 rows), a bagic-employee key (2) and a parent-party key (1); they bind to proposer. If that is wrong the attribute attaches to the wrong party. Every such binding is listed with its vote in the build report, routed to the mapper, and the rows are augmentation-track and per-column reversible. TO OVERRULE: set ANCHOR_AMBIGUOUS = 'unbuilt' in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD12-LINK-LEG-BUILT-AS-MAPPED-DIVERGENCE-MEASURED -- Where a LNK leg's expression differs from the hub key the same view resolves for that hub, the leg is built AS MAPPED and the divergence is counted at run time by audit_mtv2_link_leg_divergence. WHY: The directive asks for the hub key to be emitted for the leg 'by construction'. Doing that silently substitutes one key expression for another, which is correcting the mapping (BUILD_RULES 5.7). The two that matter are not cosmetic: on CLAIM_RESERVE the hub key walks FOREIGN_KEY and the leg walks PARENT_KEY_HASH, so choosing either changes WHICH claim the link attaches to; and 'EMP:' || BAGIC_RM_ECODE is an orphan leg no hub key anywhere produces. COST: 7 value-changing legs join to nothing until the mapper rules. That failure is silent by nature -- an empty join reads as sparse source data -- so the audit model counts legs with no matching hub row per link per view, which makes it visible without guessing. 9 further disagreements are whitespace-only and are already neutralised: render_key() normalises them to the same SQL. TO OVERRULE: set LINK_LEG_SOURCE = 'hub_key' in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD13-HUB-DOCUMENT-TWO-KEY-FORMS-BUILT-AS-MAPPED -- Where one source column keys one hub both with a namespace prefix and bare, BOTH forms are built exactly as mapped and the split is COUNTED per hub per prefix from the map in hand -- never asserted from the profile. WHY: One identifier in two key spaces is two hub rows for one document. Picking one merges populations the source has not been asked about, and merging is the unrecoverable direction by the mapper's own rule. No sample data exists to settle whether they are one population. COST: The hub carries two rows for any identifier that appears in both forms. The measured split per hub per prefix is in BUILD_STATUS.json .hub_key_forms; a zero there is a measured zero, not evidence the check works. One mapper answer collapses it. TO OVERRULE: set HUB_DOCUMENT_PREFIX = 'bare' in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD14-CHILD-KEY-COMPONENT-READER-ACCEPTS-EVERY-DECLARED-SPELLING -- The child_key_components reader accepts ALL leg-name spellings {name, leg, component, maps_to} and ALL value spellings {value, expression, raw, column, source_column}, in the profile-declared order first, and refuses `role` as a name key. Two spellings for one role on one element with DIFFERENT values is fatal. WHY: CONV-CKC-SHAPES in CONVENTIONS.json is RATIFIED and says the element shape is not fixed across runs. The profile records this build's own honouring of it as NO, and stage 0 routed the choice here: widen the reader, or state in the profile that it deliberately does not. Widening is the cheaper of the two and it is the one the declaration asks for. COST: NOTHING ON THIS MAP, and that is stated rather than implied: only name, value, leg_backing, expression, resolved_on_view, note and one `column` occur, so every new branch has ZERO live occurrences and is exercised only by the reader's own divergence probe. ck_spelling_census() prints which spellings were actually read and which were merely accepted, so the widening can never be mistaken for evidence about this bundle. The mapping side has ENDED, so no re-issue can ever exercise it either -- it is insurance with no remaining policy term, and it is implemented because a reader correct only for the bytes in front of it is the defect, not the accident. TO OVERRULE: set CK_LEG_NAME_SPELLINGS = [LEG_NAME_FIELD] (and the two sibling lists) in mtv2_keyrules.py

BD15-LINK-LEG-NAME-READER-SWEEPS-BOTH-SEPARATORS -- A LNK leg's hub name is recognised before EITHER separator, '=' or ':'. The census reports which separator named each leg, and every published link-leg figure states WHICH QUESTION it answers -- names a hub, binds to a hub, or is positional -- beside its population. WHY: MEASURED over 51 LNK( occurrences and 91 legs: 39 legs name a hub, 34 of them with '=' and 5 with ':'; 52 name no hub. An EQUALS-ONLY reader measures 34 and 57, which is where the figure '34 name a hub, 57 do not' comes from -- it is a reader defect, not a map fact, and the profile's own grammar_lnk_census declares 9 colon-form call sites that such a reader contradicts. A separate distinct-site population (30 sites, 57 legs, 23 naming a hub) supplies the SAME two digits from a third scope, which is how they were transposed onto the 91 denominator. COST: None to the build: the shipped parser already accepted both separators, so no emitted SQL changes. The cost is to the REPORT -- the published figure moves from an instructed 34/57 to a measured 39/52, and every prior figure (4, 34, 52-as-a-bare-number, 57) is listed with the scope that produced it so the next reader can tell which question each answered (BUILD_RULES 11.8). TO OVERRULE: set LNK_LEG_NAME_SEPARATORS = ('=',) in mtv2_keyrules.py and re-run; the census will report 34/57 and say so

BD16-A-PROFILE-FIGURE-IS-CROSS-CHECKED-ON-ITS-LOAD-BEARING-HALF-ONLY -- Where a profile figure is measured over a form this build does not emit, the build asserts the load-bearing property and REPORTS the arithmetic rather than asserting equality. Applied to longest_source_view_cast_name (41), to prose_test_counts.prose_columns_covered (7), and to the collapse-trap scope figures (18 / 9 / 20). WHY: An equality assertion against a figure measured over a different population is a gate that fires on correct data, and a gate that fires on correct data gets switched off (BUILD_RULES 1.12). 41 is PREFIX+stem and not the emitted model name, and it is the tied-SECOND longest even in its own form; 7 cannot be re-derived without reading the entry keys as English, which BUILD_RULES 3 forbids; the collapse-trap figures differ by SCOPE, not by fact. COST: Three profile figures are carried rather than checked, and each says so at the point of use with the population beside it. What IS asserted in their place is load-bearing: that the abbreviation vocabulary still derives the profile's example stem, that every emitted name is inside the budget, that the prose entry COUNT and its `kind` split reproduce, and that collapse-trap scope B is a subset of scope A. TO OVERRULE: in mtv2_names._probe() and build_mtv2_spec.collapse_trap_scope_reconciliation(), turn the reported comparison back into an equality check

augmented-track alignment shim -- implemented and named. OPUS travel_dv_dbt already builds 12 SAT_AUG_* satellites. 94 augmentation rows land on 9 concepts OPUS already augments, so they must be emitted INTO the OPUS-named SAT_AUG_<X> with OPUS's src_pk, single-active grain and bare HASHDIFF, extending its payload, rather than into a Maximus-side second satellite. The standard augmented layer builds per-map and cannot express that; declared exception under BUILD_RULES.md 6.5, required by 7.7.

EAV instance fan-out driven by a literal leg -- implemented and named. 593 child-key legs are pure literals naming a column-as-instance inside a pivot view. The unpivot layer must fan one parent row into N instance rows keyed by the LEG LITERAL, which has no source column to unpivot from - the literal IS the instance name. 39 of these legs carry no 'expression' field at all and the generator must synthesise the quoted literal from 'value'.

Built as mapped where it could be built, otherwise left unbuilt with the reason in build_artifacts/mtv2_spec.json. Stage 3 must put this to the mapper; the build does not correct a mapping (BUILD_RULES 5.7).
